title: Symphony No. 3 in F major
hook: Brahms’s shortest symphony grows from a three-note motto, and every movement ends quietly.

painting.title: Sunset on the Rhine
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A quiet Rhine evening painted in 1853, the autumn the young Brahms met the Schumanns in Düsseldorf on the Rhine; thirty years later, on the Rhine again, he wrote a symphony whose every movement fades into calm.

facts: Brahms wrote the symphony in the summer of 1883 in Wiesbaden, on the Rhine, six years after his Second. He was 50. The Vienna Philharmonic under Hans Richter gave the first performance in Vienna on 2 December 1883.

It opens with three rising notes, F–A-flat–F, that return all through the work. They are usually read as Brahms’s own motto, *frei aber froh*, “free but happy”, an answer to his friend Joseph Joachim’s motto *frei aber einsam*, “free but lonely”. Brahms himself never explained them.

Major and minor fight from the first bar: the motto uses the A-flat of F minor, the tune that follows the A-natural of F major. The finale starts firmly in F minor and only reaches F major in its last minutes.

It is the shortest of Brahms’s four symphonies, and all four movements end quietly, which was very unusual. Richter called it Brahms’s “Eroica”; the critic Eduard Hanslick thought it “artistically the most nearly perfect” of the symphonies so far.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a heroic, restless start that sinks to rest (I), a calm hymn for the woodwinds (II), a sad, swaying song (III), a stormy finale that finds peace (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro con brio
movements.summary: Two great chords from the winds lift the three-note [[motto|motto]], and the violins plunge down from the top in a sweeping, passionate theme. The movement is a [[sonata-form|sonata form]] full of rhythms that pull against the beat, and of sudden shadows when major turns to minor. After all its energy, it ends softly.

mainIdeas.name: The motto
mainIdeas.description: three notes, F, A-flat, F, rising in big steps; it sits under or over almost everything.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, in the violins
mainIdeas.description: two wide downward sweeps, loud and heroic, with the motto in the bass.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2, on the clarinet
mainIdeas.description: a gentle, swaying tune in a slow-feeling triple rhythm, over plucked low strings.

stops.hear: Two loud chords from the winds and brass, rising; at the top the violins sweep down in a passionate theme
stops.happening: The motto, F–A-flat–F, and Theme 1. The second chord is a sharp, uneasy one

stops.hear: Everything softens; a solo clarinet plays a graceful, swaying tune over plucked basses, a bassoon below it
stops.happening: Theme 2, in A major, a long way from home. The metre changes to 9/4

stops.hear: Dark and urgent; violins and flutes play a sad, restless melody, the rhythm seeming to start a beat too early
stops.happening: The closing theme, in A minor

stops.hear: The two rising chords and the sweeping theme again
Agitated and low: the clarinet’s tune, now in the cellos and bassoons, dark and urgent
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] begins, with Theme 2 turned into the minor

stops.hear: Calm suddenly falls; a solo horn sings the three motto notes as a slow, warm melody
stops.happening: The motto becomes a tune for the first time

stops.hear: Very quiet and slow; the low strings creep through the main theme without accompaniment
stops.happening: *Un poco sostenuto*: the way back home, in mystery

stops.hear: A sudden, loud eruption of the motto chords, now four instead of two
The heroic theme at full strength with trumpets and timpani, then a great outburst

stops.label: Last 45 seconds
stops.hear: The music calms; the motto in the winds, the violins’ sweep falling gently, a soft F major chord
stops.happening: The movement ends quietly, in the major at last

notice: Count the motto. In the first minute it is at the top of the winds, then in the bass under the violins. Once you know its shape, you hear it everywhere.
In the exposition, listen for the rhythm stumbling against the beat: the six beats of each bar often group as three twos, a kind of [[hemiola|hemiola]].

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Klemperer recorded the symphony with the Philharmonia in Kingsway Hall, London, in March 1957. He takes the repeat of the exposition, which many conductors leave out.

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: A slow, quiet movement led by the woodwinds. Clarinets and bassoons play a simple, hymn-like theme, and the low strings answer each phrase like an echo. A second, more solemn idea appears for a moment; the finale will bring it back.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a plain, folk-like melody on the clarinet, with bassoons, each phrase echoed by the low strings.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a stern, slow tune played in [[unison|unison]] by clarinet and bassoon, like a [[chorale|chorale]].

stops.hear: Clarinets and bassoons alone in a calm, simple tune; violas and cellos echo the end of each phrase
The oboe adds a decorative line; then the violins soar upwards for the first time
Clarinet and bassoon together on a bare, solemn tune; everything else falls almost silent
stops.happening: Theme 2, the chorale-like idea. Remember it for the finale

stops.hear: Short calls, each on a single note, passed between strings, woodwinds and brass
The violins burst out with the opening of the main tune; the music grows warm
The calm woodwind tune again, now with rippling strings around it
The violins sing a new, passionate melody that climbs to a warm climax and falls back
stops.happening: The emotional peak of the movement

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The clarinet’s opening notes over a held low C; a flute and oboe reach up; soft chords
stops.happening: A calm, slow close in C major

notice: Listen to the low strings after each woodwind phrase in the first minute. They answer like a congregation responding to a prayer.

movements.heading: Poco allegretto
movements.summary: Not a fast [[scherzo|scherzo]] but a melancholy song in a gentle, swaying three. The cellos sing the tune first, then the violins. In the middle comes a hazy, uncertain section for the woodwinds. When the tune returns, a solo horn has it.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a long, sad melody in C minor, first in the cellos, over a quietly flowing accompaniment.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: soft woodwind chords that seem to fall off the beat, with a sighing line in the cellos.

stops.hear: The cellos sing a sad, swaying melody; the other strings flow softly beneath
stops.happening: The main theme, in C minor

stops.hear: The violins take the melody, an octave higher
Warmer and in the major; cellos and violins together in a tender, arching line
Flute, oboe and horn play the melody together
Woodwind chords that seem to land off the beat; the cellos sigh below them
stops.happening: The middle section, the [[trio|trio]], in A-flat

stops.hear: The strings alone, a gently swaying, richer phrase
stops.happening: A song for the strings inside the middle section

stops.hear: A solo horn sings the opening melody
stops.happening: The main section returns, in a new colour

stops.hear: The oboe takes the melody
Violins and cellos together, the melody spread over three octaves

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: Soft, held chords and a quiet fall to the end

notice: Follow the melody from cellos to violins, then horn, oboe, and finally violins and cellos together. The tune stays the same; the colour changes each time.

movements.heading: Allegro – Un poco sostenuto
movements.summary: The finale begins in a whisper, in F minor, and soon turns into a storm. The solemn chorale from the second movement breaks in twice. The coda slows down, settles into F major, and in the last bars the main theme of the first movement returns, now soft and shimmering.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a hushed, scurrying theme in the strings and bassoons, in unison.

mainIdeas.name: The chorale
mainIdeas.description: the solemn tune from the second movement, now in the trombones.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a heroic, striding tune for cellos and horn, in triplets.

stops.hear: Strings and bassoons in unison, very quiet, on a nervous, turning theme
Trombones enter softly on one note; then a solemn, quiet tune
stops.happening: The chorale from the second movement returns

stops.hear: A sudden, loud outburst from the full orchestra
A bold, striding tune in cellos and horn
Fierce and dramatic, hammered rhythms across the orchestra
stops.happening: The closing theme, in C minor

stops.hear: The opening theme quietly in the woodwinds over plucked strings
A dramatic silence, then the chorale blazes out loud, with swirling strings around it
The striding tune again, now in F major
stops.happening: Theme 2 returns in the home key

stops.hear: Slower; the violas play the opening theme in a calm, rocking rhythm
Shimmering strings; the music has turned to F major
Over a shimmer of strings, the violins play the first movement’s sweeping theme, softly
stops.happening: The opening theme of the symphony returns

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: A quiet, glowing F major chord, held

notice: Listen for the trombones’ quiet entry near the start. It is the tune from the second movement, and it will return twice.
In the very last minute, listen for the first movement’s sweeping theme in the violins. It began loud and heroic; it ends as a soft glow.

threads.title: The motto
threads.body: F–A-flat–F opens the symphony and runs through the first movement; in the last bars of the finale it lifts the music once more before the first movement’s theme returns.

threads.title: Major and minor
threads.body: A-flat against A, F minor against F major. The struggle that begins in the first bar is only settled in the finale’s coda.

threads.title: Quiet endings
threads.body: Each movement ends softly. The finale, with all its storm, does the same: Brahms closes the symphony with calm, not triumph.

threads.title: Themes that return
threads.body: The second movement’s chorale comes back in the finale, and the first movement’s theme closes the whole work. Brahms built this symphony as one journey.
